newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas called up on heat, firmer power prices.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas called up on heat, firmer power prices.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open higher Tuesday in continuance of Monday's rally on hot weather across most of the U.S. and stronger electricity prices, sources said.
August over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.17 to $2.18 after settling to the upside Monday at $2.151 per million British thermal units.

"Electricity is screaming. As a result, gas is moving higher," one trader said, noting peak prices were talked early around $90 per megawatt hour (MWh) in the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) and as high as $100 per MWh in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT).
August continued to gain strength on ACCESS by breaking through the $2.155 resistance level to a high of $2.167, up 1.6 cents from the afternoon settlement.
Chart traders said next August resistance was along the down trendline at $2.23-24. Support was seen at last week's $2.051 low, with psychological buying likely at $2.

In Monday's cash, Gulf Coast prices firmed two to three cents to the mid-teens. Midcon pipes were up a similar amount to $2.05-2.06, while New York city gate gas jumped more than five cents to the mid-to-high $2.40s.
Early Tuesday cash prices at the Henry Hub were talked a few cents higher around $2.20.
Supporting cash and futures in the near-term have been the above-normal temperatures stretching across most of the U.S., traders said.

By the latter part of the week and into early next week, however, forecasts are calling for normal to below-normal temperatures in the eastern half of the U.S., including Texas and the southern plains.
Separately, early estimates for Wednesday's American Gas Association storage report are about 78 bcf.
